Non-classical Monocyte.description: Non-classical monocytes are CD16+CD14- patrolling monocytes that survey the endothelium and respond to viral infections, characterized by high expression of FCGR3A and low CD14.

Classical Monocyte.description: Classical monocytes are CD14+CD16- phagocytic cells that produce inflammatory cytokines and express high CD14, S100A8/S100A9, and CSF1R.

Intermediate Monocyte.description: Intermediate monocytes are CD14+CD16+ cells that exhibit both classical and non-classical features, with high levels of CD14 and FCGR3A, and produce pro-inflammatory cytokines.

NK Cell.description: Natural killer cells are innate lymphoid cells that kill virally infected and tumor cells, expressing NKG7, GZMB, PRF1, and FCGR3A (CD16).

Myeloid Dendritic Cell.description: Myeloid dendritic cells are professional antigen-presenting cells that express CLEC10A, FCER1A, CD1C, and high levels of MHC class II molecules.

Classical Monocytes.description: Classical monocytes (CD14++CD16-) are the most abundant monocyte subset in PBMC, characterized by high expression of CD14 and chemokine receptor CCR2, and they play key roles in phagocytosis and inflammation.

Intermediate Monocytes.description: Intermediate monocytes (CD14++CD16+) co-express high levels of CD14 and CD16, along with MHC class II molecules, and are associated with antigen presentation and proinflammatory cytokine production.

Non-classical Monocytes.description: Non-classical monocytes (CD14+CD16++) express low CD14 and high CD16 (FcγRIII), patrol the vasculature, and are involved in immune surveillance and tissue repair.

Myeloid Dendritic Cells.description: Myeloid dendritic cells (mDCs) are professional antigen-presenting cells in PBMC, expressing high levels of MHC class II and specific markers like CD1c and FCER1A, and are crucial for initiating T-cell responses.

Plasmacytoid Dendritic Cells.description: Plasmacytoid dendritic cells (pDCs) are specialized in type I interferon production upon viral recognition, expressing high levels of CD123 (IL3RA), CLEC4C, and TLR7/9.
